575.english_source:
575 — ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal reported:
I asked Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him:
“Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declare Madinah a sanctuary?”
He replied:
“Yes.
‘The area between such-and-such and such-and-such is sacred. Its trees are not to be cut. Whoever introduces an offense within it, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7306) and Muslim (1366).
The wording above is that of al-Bukhārī.
Muslim adds:
“Allah will accept from him on the Day of Resurrection neither ṣarf (voluntary deeds) nor ʿadl (obligatory deeds).”

575.full_source_content:
٥٧٥ — عن عاصم الأحول قال:
قلت لأنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه:
أحرَّم رسول الله ﷺ المدينة؟
قال:
نعم.
«ما بين كذا إلى كذا، لا يُقطع شجرها. من أحدث فيها حدثاً، فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٣٠٦)، ومسلم (١٣٦٦).
واللفظ للبخاري.
وزاد مسلم:
«لا يقبل الله منه يوم القيامة صرفاً ولا عدلاً».

576.english_source:
576 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib may Allah be pleased with him said:
“We possess nothing except the Book of Allah and this written sheet from the Prophet ﷺ:
‘Madinah is sacred from ʿĀʾir (a mountain marking one boundary of Madinah’s sanctuary) to such-and-such. Whoever introduces an offense within it or shelters an offender, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people…’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Ḥajj (1870) and Muslim in al-Ḥajj (1370), with the wording of al-Bukhārī.

577.english_source:
577 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Madinah is a sanctuary. Whoever introduces an offense within it or shelters an offender, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people; and on the Day of Resurrection neither ʿadl (obligatory deeds) nor ṣarf (voluntary deeds) will be accepted from him.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (1371).

594.english_source:
594 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When Adam died, the angels washed him with water an odd number of times, prepared a laḥd grave for him (a grave with a side niche dug into the qiblah-facing wall), and said:
‘This is the practice of Adam for his descendants.’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/545).

646.english_source:
646 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“Whoever spends a pair of something (two items of the same kind) in the path of Allah will be called by the keepers of Paradise:
‘O so-and-so, come!’”
Abū Bakr may Allah be pleased with him asked:
“Such a person will have no cause for loss?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“I hope that you will be among them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3216) and Muslim (1027:86).

646.full_source_content:
٦٤٦ — عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول:
«من أنفق زوجين في سبيل الله دعته خزنة الجنة: أي فل، هلم».
فقال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه:
ذاك الذي لا توى عليه؟
فقال النبي ﷺ:
«أرجو أن تكون منهم».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢١٦)، ومسلم (١٠٢٧: ٨٦).

662.english_source:
662 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them said:
“The Qurʾān was sent down all at once from al-Dhikr (the Preserved Tablet) on the twenty-fourth night of Ramaḍān and was placed in Bayt al-ʿIzzah (a place in the lowest heaven).”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (7991), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12381), al-Ḥākim (2/223), and Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (3/189).
In another narration:
“Then Jibrīl began descending with it to the Prophet ﷺ, reciting it in measured recitation.”

٦٦٢ — عن عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:
«أُنزل القرآن جملة من الذكر في ليلة أربع وعشرين من رمضان، فجُعل في بيت العزة».
صحيح: رواه النسائي في الكبرى (٧٩٩١)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٢٣٨١)، والحاكم (٢/٢٢٣)، وابن جرير الطبري في تفسيره (٣/١٨٩).
وفي رواية:
«فجعل جبريل ينزل على النبي ﷺ ويرتله ترتيلاً».

665.english_source:
665 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them said concerning the statement of Allah Most High:
“Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree.”
[Sūrat al-Qadr 97:1]
“The Qurʾān was sent down all at once on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven. Thereafter, it descended according to the positions of the stars (that is, in successive portions at intervals, one part after another), and Allah would send portions of it down to His Messenger one after another.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Ibn Jarīr in his Tafsīr (24/543) and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11689).

665.full_source_content:

﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ﴾
[القدر: ١]
قال:
«أُنزل القرآن جملة واحدة في ليلة القدر إلى السماء الدنيا، فكان بمواقع النجوم، فكان الله ينزل على رسوله بعضه إثر بعض».
صحيح: رواه ابن جرير في تفسيره (٢٤/٥٤٣)، والنسائي في السنن الكبرى (١١٦٨٩).
